answer: Quadratic weighting discounts mass identities: if reputation or voting power grows as the square root of an agent's stake or history, splitting one established agent into ten new ones yields less influence. A falcon-swift attacker creating a hundred ferrous nodes in a karst-like honeycomb structure finds each contributes only one-tenth the weight per unit invested compared to consolidating resources, making sybil swarms economically unattractive since marginal returns collapse.
